metadata.jurisdiction_note: County/CUPA not resolved; conclusion relies on federal SPCC threshold and lack of petroleum/oil fact.

sources: 40 CFR 112.1(b), eCFR API version 2026-06-01: applies to owners/operators of non-transportation-related facilities storing/using oil that could reasonably discharge to navigable waters and that have oil in aboveground/buried containers.

40 CFR 112.1(d)(2)(ii), eCFR API version 2026-06-01: part 112 does not apply where aggregate aboveground storage capacity is 1,320 U.S. gallons or less; only containers with capacity of 55 U.S. gallons or greater are counted.
40 CFR 112.1(d)(5), eCFR API version 2026-06-01: part 112 does not apply to any container with storage capacity of less than 55 gallons of oil.

40 CFR 112.2, eCFR API version 2026-06-01: “Oil” includes fats, oils, greases, vegetable oils, and “other oils and greases, including petroleum, fuel oil, sludge, synthetic oils, mineral oils, oil refuse…”; “Petroleum oil” means petroleum in any form including crude oil, fuel oil, mineral oil, sludge, oil refuse, and refined products.
summary: APSA/SPCC applicability is not established on the provided facts. The project describes storage of 60 gallons of flammable solvent at a coating shop, not petroleum/oil storage. Even if the solvent were an oil/petroleum product, the federal SPCC threshold excludes facilities with aggregate aboveground oil storage capacity of 1,320 U.S. gallons or less, counting only containers 55 gallons or larger; 60 gallons is far below 1,320 gallons. Therefore, on the stated facts, an APSA/SPCC plan/permit obligation is unlikely. Confirm whether the solvent is petroleum oil or otherwise an “oil” and whether the facility has other aboveground oil containers that would raise aggregate capacity to >1,320 gallons.
title: H-HAZMAT-APSA: 60 gal solvent storage is not enough by itself to trigger APSA/SPCC oil-storage applicability
